budget.time_policy: caller-owned wall-clock cancellation; pure boundary enforces deterministic validation steps

determinism.accounting: input, output, candidate, entity, delta, path, string, integer, nesting, graph, validation-step, and memory-policy ceilings are checked before corresponding retention, traversal, sorting, fragment construction, serialization, or hashing work
determinism.canonicalization: intake and ProblemIR bytes are revalidated without rewriting; projection and result JSON use NFC strings, sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, no floats, and exactly one trailing LF
determinism.identity: input-result, ProblemIR, projection, fragment, and result identities are full lowercase SHA-256 of complete canonical bytes; object identity, hash(), repr(), pickle, process, checkout path, locale, and platform never contribute
determinism.ordering: candidate wrappers and registries sort by stable ID; set-valued IDs and paths sort and deduplicate; declared difference order and every ProblemIR semantic order are preserved exactly
determinism.portability: the same canonical accepted intake bytes produce byte-identical analyzed or failed results across repeated processes, Python hash seeds, supported Python 3.10 through 3.14 interpreters, and Linux, macOS, and Windows

effects.filesystem: none; analyze_problem_readings opens no schema, contract, source document, path, configuration, cache, environment file, plugin, or repository artifact
effects.mutation: input bytes and parsed intake values are never mutated or retained by mutable alias; result values own immutable exact scalars, tuples, canonical bytes, and reconstructed read-only views
effects.network: none; no remote parser, model, proof service, catalog, package index, telemetry, or external resolver is consulted
effects.process: none; no subprocess, worker, shell, executable lookup, signal, clock, environment, randomness, locale query, dynamic import, filesystem adapter, CLI, MCP, or notebook operation occurs
effects.solver: none; no solver, CAS, discovery producer, proof producer, checker, proof assistant, evaluator, simplifier, natural-language parser, or legacy reasoning module is imported or invoked

ensures: analyze_problem_readings returns one closed immutable ReadingAnalysisResult with status analyzed, invalid, or exhausted; ordinary malformed input never returns a partial candidate, partial projection, partial delta, partial digest, or authority-bearing exception.

Before analysis the function reparses and completely revalidates the canonical intake result, its accepted-only state, its full input-result SHA-256, its embedded canonical ProblemIR bytes, its ProblemIR SHA-256, and every frozen contract and schema binding.

An analyzed result identifies exactly one base reading, requires every alternative to link directly to that base, sorts candidate wrappers by reading ID, preserves declared delta order with stable ordinals, and rejects self-links, alternative chains, cycles, duplicate candidates, unknown candidates, or multiple bases rather than repairing them.

Each candidate contains one canonical mathhead.reading-projection.v2 object conforming to docs/contracts/schemas/reading-projection-v2.schema.json=99ce60e50472e4c9d8026e9af361e4d7b11c776e577aa57de46794998fb26241 and the full lowercase SHA-256 of its exact canonical UTF-8 JSON bytes with sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, no floats, and one trailing LF.

A reading projection retains the exact reading label, root definition and assumption sets, semantic ordered goal list, reading spans, global extensions, and the complete transitive closure of every reachable definition, assumption, goal, statement, relation, expression, variable, domain, source span, and source document; registries and set-valued IDs sort while goal, binder, argument, operand, tuple, and parameter order remains semantic.

The base candidate contains no deltas. Every alternative contains one output delta per declared ProblemIR difference, preserving kind and normalized summary while independently recomputing removed, added, and retained affected IDs, structural paths, source spans, and before/after canonical fragment SHA-256 values.

No structurally changed root or closure ID is omitted from the union of alternative affected IDs, no unaffected ID is classified as added or removed, and a retained affected ID is accepted only when its ordered-goal position or source-anchored reading evidence actually differs; empty, false, surplus, duplicate, or dangling difference metadata fails closed.

A quantifier delta is emitted only when reachable quantified statements and their quantifier, binder order, domains, or bodies differ; a domain delta is emitted only when reachable domain records or domain references differ; scope and reference deltas require corresponding ownership, reachability, or edge changes; notation and parse deltas require source-span evidence and never assert semantic equivalence; other covers only remaining demonstrated structural change.

Unambiguous analysis has one base candidate, preserves its declared selection, and has no required choice; unresolved analysis has at least two candidates, no selected reading, and one required-choice object copying the exact prompt and complete sorted candidates; resolved analysis retains at least two candidates and only the already-declared selected reading, with no required-choice object.

An invalid or exhausted result contains no embedded intake result, ProblemIR identity, ambiguity state, base, selection, required choice, candidate, projection, or delta and contains one bounded stable diagnostic; mathematical_authority is false for every status.

An analyzed result embeds the complete accepted mathhead.problem-intake-result.v1 object as intake_result. Canonical serialization of that object is byte-identical to the function input and hashes to input_result_sha256, so historical analyzed results remain self-contained and independently replayable.

The result conforms to docs/contracts/schemas/problem-readings-result-v2.schema.json=b05b16d280260ac7854477274852f0273e0a6cb011d740ae827ca172dad72894, binds this contract plus the accepted intake and ProblemIR contracts, has canonical deterministic result bytes and a recomputed result SHA-256, and can be consumed only after complete result revalidation.

Construction does not parse or infer from prose, Markdown, LaTeX, MathML, Python expressions, SymPy, labels, summaries, CLI text, MCP payloads, or legacy discovery output; it does not synthesize a reading, choose a candidate, infer a domain or assumption, normalize semantics, solve, prove, call a checker, or issue any trust tier.

ReadingAnalysisResult has constructor-controlled closed values, final subclass behavior, frozen slots, blocked pickle authority, copy-safe identity, canonical parse and serialization boundaries, and complete recomputation before an analyzed result is consumed.

epistemics.analyzed: every already-declared reading has a deterministic complete structural projection and every declared alternative difference has independently recomputed structural evidence; no reading is preferred and no mathematical truth is claimed
epistemics.exhausted: a finite byte, structure, graph, delta, path, validation-work, or memory-policy ceiling was exceeded before complete analysis; no partial projection or identity is returned
epistemics.invalid: the input intake artifact, reading topology, declared difference, classification, projection, canonical form, or binding is invalid and yields bounded diagnostics without a ProblemIR or projection identity
epistemics.non_authoritative: analysis records representation differences only; mathematical_authority is always false and labels, summaries, hashes, or successful structure checks cannot issue evidence or a trust tier
epistemics.required_choice: unresolved ambiguity retains all candidates, no selected reading, and the exact explicit caller-authored choice prompt; the function cannot answer that prompt

invariants: The projection schema is docs/contracts/schemas/reading-projection-v2.schema.json=99ce60e50472e4c9d8026e9af361e4d7b11c776e577aa57de46794998fb26241 and the result schema is docs/contracts/schemas/problem-readings-result-v2.schema.json=b05b16d280260ac7854477274852f0273e0a6cb011d740ae827ca172dad72894; unknown fields fail closed at every object boundary.

The production module depends only on the standard library and the accepted mathhead.problem_intake boundary and imports no third-party, natural-language or legacy parser, NLP or model, solver, CAS, discovery producer, checker, proof assistant, filesystem, process, network, clock, environment, randomness, dynamic-import, worker, CLI, MCP, notebook, or transport owner.

Canonical accepted intake bytes are the sole source of candidates. Text, labels, difference summaries, extensions, legacy reading envelopes, result-like objects, caller-supplied projections, caller-supplied hashes, and adapter payloads cannot add, remove, classify, or select a reading.

The base reading is the sole candidate whose difference_from is null; every alternative points directly to it and has at least one declared and recomputed nonempty delta; a base never carries a delta.

Projection closure begins only at the reading definition, assumption, and ordered goal roots and follows every typed ProblemIR dependency plus all entity and reading source spans to source documents. Unreachable global entities are excluded and reachable entities cannot be omitted.

Projection entity registries, definition and assumption sets, span sets, entity IDs, delta affected/removed/added/retained IDs, and paths are strictly sorted and unique. Reading goal order, binder order, expression and relation operands, logical operands, tuple elements, function arguments, and definition parameters remain semantic.

Every projection identity changes if its reading roots, semantic order, reachable entity bytes, source provenance, label, base identity, or global extension annotations change; every result identity changes if any binding, state, choice, candidate, projection, delta, diagnostic, or authority field changes.

Delta removed IDs occur only in the base closure, added IDs occur only in the alternative closure, retained IDs occur in both, and their union equals affected IDs. Before or after fragment hashes are null exactly when that side has no affected structural material.

Quantifier, domain, and scope classifiers inspect exact typed records and graph ownership, not names or summaries. Notation and parse kinds require declared source spans bounded by accepted source identities and remain claims about representation provenance only.

Unambiguous, unresolved, and resolved output combinations exactly mirror the accepted ProblemIR ambiguity state and never reinterpret it. An unresolved result cannot contain a selection and a resolved or unambiguous result cannot contain a required-choice object.

Failed and exhausted combinations cannot contain an embedded intake result, ProblemIR or projection identities, candidates, deltas, selections, or required choices; analyzed cannot contain diagnostics; all combinations are recomputed during strict result parsing.

Strict parsing of analyzed result bytes reconstructs the embedded canonical intake bytes, reparses the accepted intake artifact, reruns analyze_problem_readings from that artifact under this exact contract, and requires byte-identical output; a fabricated projection, delta, binding, input hash, or ProblemIR hash therefore fails closed even if outer hashes are repaired.

All strings are NUL-free NFC, integers exclude bool and stay in the portable exact range, arrays and graphs remain within their fixed ceilings, and subclasses, object.__new__, setattr, replace, copy, deepcopy, pickle, duplicate JSON keys, floats, and noncanonical encodings cannot forge analyzed state.

Analyzed output is structural representation evidence only and mathematical_authority is always false. No choice, normalization, solver verdict, checker attestation, certificate, proof term, external proof, or trust transition is created or preserved by this boundary.
raises: Ordinary wrong types, malformed intake bytes, invalid or exhausted intake states, forged bindings, stale hashes, noncanonical encodings, invalid reading topology, false or incomplete differences, unsupported classifications, and deterministic budget exhaustion return invalid or exhausted ReadingAnalysisResult values with no projection identity.

ReadingAnalysisValidationError with stable kind type, schema, canonical, identity, result, or budget is raised only by explicitly requested strict result parsing, canonical result serialization, projection serialization, or hashing boundaries receiving forged, stale, malformed, noncanonical, or over-budget result data.

PermissionError is raised for direct public construction of result values; TypeError is raised for subclass and pickle attempts; copy operations either preserve the same closed value identity or fail.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate and can never be converted into analyzed, selected, normalized, valid, proved, verified, or otherwise authority-bearing output.
requires: The accepted MH-C-WORKFLOW-001=99cfdf17371938af65c4203c02cbaac0bf73470e9fab59f7a6d62360fc0b7cca governs this critical public interpretation-analysis boundary.

The accepted MH-C-PROBLEM-INTAKE-001=855375a8fb788ff65728d860c16f0ccfa32fe9d058b3fe93534ef11f147794dc and result schema docs/contracts/schemas/problem-intake-result-v1.schema.json=0ea174a09391dd7f690bba9df7dfd08d8f1253032c472ca60d45eaf9f47101d3 define the sole input artifact and its canonical parser.

The accepted MH-C-PROBLEM-IR-002=6d657195869a5746c5a41492c334b32ee5edd2ca84eb7facfade44f53334c286 and schema docs/contracts/schemas/problem-ir-v1.schema.json=dcf871f15ebbae06b0eca285a115f2545defc00cb0befc23e3cc574d8523df2c define all reading, difference, ambiguity, entity, ordering, reference, scope, and source-span semantics.

intake_result is an exact built-in bytes value containing one complete canonical mathhead.problem-intake-result.v1 object with status accepted, mathematical_authority false, no diagnostics, exact contract bindings, exact ProblemIR bytes, and recomputable identities; malformed, invalid, exhausted, forged, stale, noncanonical, subclassed, or over-budget inputs are rejected without analysis.

The accepted ProblemIR contains at least one complete reading, exactly one reading whose difference_from is null, an ambiguity candidate list naming every reading exactly once, and the status, selection, and required-choice combination required by MH-C-PROBLEM-IR-002.

The caller treats analyzed output as a deterministic comparison of already-declared representations only, not as natural-language interpretation, semantic equivalence, domain normalization, proof, refutation, solver evidence, checker evidence, or permission to bypass later validation.
